## Loading GGUF models

You name a model by its Hub repo id, such as `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-GGUF`, and
rishi picks the file. The constants below are ready-made repo ids. Qwen3
models can think before answering and write tool calls in a format
llama.cpp already parses. Any GGUF repo works.

A repo often holds one file per quantization, plus an `mmproj` file.
That file is the projector, a small separate model that turns images or
audio into input the language model can read.
[`get_model`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#get_model)
finds the model file in three steps. It uses a `model_path` you pass if
the file exists. Otherwise it searches the local Hugging Face cache
without using the network. Otherwise it downloads the file. It prefers
the `quant` you ask for, `Q4_K_M` by default, and falls back to the
first `.gguf` file. It never picks the projector. It raises
`FileNotFoundError` when the repo has no model file.
[`cached_model`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#cached_model)
is the cache step on its own and returns None on a miss. The old names
`_get_model` and `_cached_model` still work.
[`get_mmproj`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/llama.html#get_mmproj)
finds the projector the same way, for vision and audio models. It raises
`FileNotFoundError` when the repo has no projector. `DFLT_N_CTX` is the
context window an engine gets when nothing else sets one, 8192 tokens.

[`gpu_offload_supported`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/llama.html#gpu_offload_supported)
says whether the installed llama-cpp-python wheel was built with Metal
or CUDA. A CPU-only wheel ignores `n_gpu_layers`.

## Audio

llama.cpp reads images and audio through its mtmd library, but
llama-cpp-python’s `MTMDChatHandler` only passes images to it. rishi
patches four of the handler’s methods so that audio takes the same
route:

- `get_image_urls` collects `input_audio` parts as well as images, in
  the order they appear.
- `_get_template_messages` replaces each image or audio part with a
  marker. When only text parts remain, it joins them into one string.
  Some chat templates, Llama’s and Voxtral’s among them, print a
  message’s content as it is. Without the join they would print a Python
  list.
- `_create_bitmap_from_bytes` decodes audio with
  [`read_audio`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/llama.html#read_audio)
  and hands the samples to `mtmd_bitmap_init_from_audio`. Images take
  the original path.
- `_init_mtmd_context` lets a projector with an audio encoder and no
  vision encoder load, where upstream raises an error.

[`read_audio`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/llama.html#read_audio)
decodes any format libsndfile reads, including WAV, FLAC, OGG and MP3.
It mixes stereo down to mono and resamples to `sr` Hz, 16000 by default.
The patched `_create_bitmap_from_bytes` passes the sample rate the
projector reports, and falls back to 16000 when the projector reports
none. The tests below run it on the 24-second `speech.wav` and on
generated tones, and pass the result to the real llama.cpp C function.

``` python
import io
from fastcore.all import Path
from contextlib import ExitStack
from llama_cpp import mtmd_cpp
import tempfile
```

``` python
# read_audio decodes the real 24s clip and resamples it, preserving duration
wav = Path('speech.wav').read_bytes()
a = read_audio(wav, 16000)
test_eq(a.dtype, np.dtype('float32'))
assert a.flags['C_CONTIGUOUS'] and -1.0 <= a.min() and a.max() <= 1.0
test_eq(round(len(a) / 16000), 24)                       # 24s in, 24s out
test_eq(round(len(read_audio(wav, 8000)) / 8000), 24)    # and at a different target rate

# soundfile handles compressed containers too, not just WAV
sig = (0.2 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 220 * np.arange(8000) / 8000)).astype(np.float32)
for fmt in ('FLAC', 'OGG', 'MP3'):
    b = io.BytesIO(); sf.write(b, sig, 8000, format=fmt)
    d = read_audio(b.getvalue(), 8000)
    test_eq(d.dtype, np.dtype('float32')); assert d.flags['C_CONTIGUOUS'], fmt
    assert abs(len(d) - 8000) <= 2400, (fmt, len(d))     # ~1s back; lossy codecs pad a little

# stereo is downmixed to mono
st = np.stack([sig, np.zeros_like(sig)], axis=1)
b = io.BytesIO(); sf.write(b, st, 8000, format='WAV', subtype='FLOAT')
test_eq(read_audio(b.getvalue(), 8000).ndim, 1)

test_fail(lambda: read_audio(b'not audio at all'), contains='could not decode audio')
```

``` python
# a template that renders `content` directly (Llama/Voxtral-style) must get a STRING, not a list repr:
# _get_template_messages collapses media+text to a clean string with the marker inline
h = object.__new__(MTMDChatHandler)
msg = {'role': 'user', 'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': 'Transcribe this clip.'},
                                   {'type': 'input_audio', 'input_audio': {'data': 'AAA', 'format': 'wav'}}]}
conv = h._get_template_messages([msg], '<M>')[0]['content']
test_eq(conv, 'Transcribe this clip.\n<M>')
assert isinstance(conv, str)   # never a Python list repr
# a plain-string message is passed through untouched
test_eq(h._get_template_messages([{'role': 'user', 'content': 'hi'}], '<M>')[0]['content'], 'hi')
```

``` python
# the patched handler collects image *and* audio media, in document order
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.gguf') as f:
    h = MTMDChatHandler(f.name, verbose=False)
    img = Path('images.jpeg').read_bytes()
    msgs = [_mk_msg([img, 'and this?', wav])]
    urls = h.get_image_urls(msgs)
    test_eq(len(urls), 2)
    assert urls[0].startswith('data:image/jpeg;base64,') and urls[1].startswith('data:audio/wav;base64,')

    # every media part becomes the marker; text is left alone
    # media parts become the marker and the all-text content collapses to a clean string (marker inline)
    test_eq(h._get_template_messages(msgs, '<__media__>')[0]['content'], '<__media__>\nand this?\n<__media__>')

    # and the data-URI round-trips back to the exact bytes the model will decode
    test_eq(h.load_image(urls[1]), wav)
    test_eq(h.load_image(urls[0]), img)
```

``` python
# the decoded buffer is accepted by real llama.cpp: `mtmd_bitmap_init_from_audio` needs no
# context or model, so the actual C boundary is exercised here rather than mocked
bm = mtmd_cpp.mtmd_bitmap_init_from_audio(len(a), a.ctypes.data_as(ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_float)))
assert bm is not None, 'llama.cpp rejected the audio buffer'
try:
    assert mtmd_cpp.mtmd_bitmap_is_audio(bm)
    test_eq(mtmd_cpp.mtmd_bitmap_get_n_bytes(bm), len(a) * 4)     # float32 per sample
    back = np.ctypeslib.as_array(ctypes.cast(mtmd_cpp.mtmd_bitmap_get_data(bm),
                                             ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_float)), shape=(len(a),))
    assert np.array_equal(back, a), 'samples corrupted crossing the C boundary'
finally: mtmd_cpp.mtmd_bitmap_free(bm)
```

## LlamaChat

`LlamaChat(model)` loads the model once and keeps it for the life of the
chat. `create_engine` builds the `llama_cpp.Llama` object and adds the
multimodal handler when `mmproj` is set. Pass `mmproj=True` to fetch the
projector from the same repo, or a path to use your own.

The options particular to llama.cpp are `quant`, the quantization to
download; `n_gpu_layers`, how many layers go on the GPU, where 0 (the
default) keeps everything on the CPU; and `mmproj`. `think=True` or
`think=False` writes Qwen’s `/think` or `/no_think` switch into the
system prompt. To share one loaded model between chats, build it once
with `create_engine` and pass it to each as `engine=`. `close` releases
an engine the chat built itself and leaves a shared `engine=` open.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/rishi/blob/main/rishi/llama.py#L159"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### LlamaChat

``` python
def LlamaChat(
    model:NoneType=None, *, runtime:NoneType=None, model_path:NoneType=None, opts:NoneType=None,
    engine:NoneType=None, # an engine to share instead of building one
    quant:str='Q4_K_M', # which GGUF quantization to fetch
    n_gpu_layers:int=0, mmproj:NoneType=None, # the projector image and audio input need
    eng_kw:NoneType=None, # passed to `create_engine` verbatim
    preserve_cache:bool=False, comp_kw:NoneType=None, # passed to `create_chat_completion` verbatim
    **kw
):
```

*A `Chat` that runs a GGUF model inside this process through
llama-cpp-python.*

### The KV cache

While a model reads a prompt, it computes a key and a value for every
token, and llama.cpp keeps them in the KV cache. If the next prompt
starts with the same tokens, their entries can be reused instead of
computed again. Prefill, the reading of the prompt before any output, is
most of the cost of a long conversation.

rishi reuses the cache by keeping one `Llama` object across turns.
`Llama.generate` compares each new prompt with the tokens already in its
context, trims the cache back to the longest common prefix, and
evaluates only what follows. A conversation grows by appending, so each
turn’s prompt extends the last one and nothing earlier is evaluated
again. The manual example below shows it: on the second turn llama.cpp
evaluated 28 new tokens and reused 315.

Three things break the prefix, and `cached_tokens` takes all three into
account:

- A one-shot call on the same engine. A `Llama` has a single context, so
  `classify`, `structured`, `check` and `grades` overwrite the
  conversation in it, and the next real turn starts from scratch. Two
  chats sharing one `engine=`, or a judge chat on the same engine, have
  the same effect. With `preserve_cache=True` the chat saves the llama
  state before a one-shot and restores it afterwards. That copies the
  whole cache. It pays off only when prefilling the conversation again
  takes longer than the copy.
- A rewritten history. When `SlidingWindowCallback` drops old messages,
  or context recovery shortens the history, everything after the first
  changed message is evaluated again.
- Media. The turn that carries an image or audio clip sends the real
  thing. On later turns an `[image]` or `[audio]` placeholder replaces
  it, and llama.cpp does not encode it again. The replacement changes
  the prompt from that message on. The turn after a media turn evaluates
  again from there.

`save_cache` writes the whole context to a file, and `load_cache` reads
it back into a chat built on the same model. The method names match
`rishi.mlx`. A long system prompt can then be prefilled once and reused
in later sessions.

### Recorded model behaviour

These checks run against replies recorded from the real `qwen3_06b`
model. Urai’s `CachedChat` replays a recorded reply when it sees the
same request again, and a replay builds no engine, so the tests check
rishi’s handling of real llama.cpp output without loading the model.
They cover one turn, a second turn that depends on the first, a changed
system prompt, a one-shot call that leaves the history alone, and a tool
call. The recordings live in `nbs/chatcache`, and the checks work on a
temporary copy so the originals stay unchanged.

``` python
c = CachedChat(**_llama_record_kw)
r = c('Reply with exactly: pong')
test_eq(resp_text(r).strip().lower(), 'pong')
test_eq([m['role'] for m in c.hist], ['user', 'assistant'])
c.close()
```

``` python
c = CachedChat(**_llama_record_kw)
c('Reply with exactly: pong')
r = c('What exact word did you just reply with? Reply with only that word.')
test_eq(resp_text(r).strip().lower(), 'pong')
test_eq([m['role'] for m in c.hist], ['user', 'assistant', 'user', 'assistant'])
c.close()
```

``` python
c = CachedChat(**_llama_record_kw)
c.reconfigure(sp='Reply with exactly the word anchor, whatever the user asks.')
test_eq(resp_text(c('What is two plus two?')).strip().lower(), 'anchor')
c.close()
```

``` python
c = CachedChat(**_llama_record_kw)
test_eq(c.oneshot('Reply with exactly: solo', think=False, max_tokens=16).strip().lower(), 'solo')
test_eq(c.hist, [])
c.close()
```

``` python
def add(
    a: int,  # first addend
    b: int,  # second addend
) -> int:
    "Add two integers."
    return a + b

c = CachedChat(**{**_llama_record_kw, 'max_output_tokens': 128}, tools=[add])
r = c('Use the add tool to add 2 and 3. Reply with only the result.')
test_eq(c.hist[1]['tool_calls'][0]['function']['name'], 'add')
test_eq(c.hist[2]['content'], '5')
assert '5' in resp_text(r)
c.close()
```

The tests above cover choosing the GGUF file, the GPU check, audio
decoding, the handler patches and the recorded turns. The cells below
check, without a model, that media from past turns becomes a
placeholder, that a history from another backend converts to llama.cpp’s
format, and that `Chat` picks
[`LlamaChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/llama.html#llamachat)
for a GGUF name.

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq
# _strip_media collapses past-turn media to a text placeholder; plain strings pass through untouched (pure fn, no model)
test_eq(_strip_media({'role': 'user', 'content': 'plain'}), {'role': 'user', 'content': 'plain'})
past = {'role': 'user', 'content': [{'type': 'input_audio', 'input_audio': {'data': 'x', 'format': 'wav'}},
                                    {'type': 'text', 'text': 'clip 1'}]}
test_eq(_strip_media(past)['content'], '[audio]\nclip 1')
assert _is_media({'type': 'image_url', 'image_url': {'url': 'data:img'}})
assert not _is_media({'type': 'text', 'text': 'hi'})
```

``` python
# hist2fmt / fmt2hist across backends (model-free): a litert-origin canonical tool round feeds llama.cpp
_h = [
    {'role': 'user', 'content': 'What is 2+3?'},
    {'role': 'assistant', 'content': '', 'tool_calls': [{'id': 'call_1', 'type': 'function',
                                                         'function': {'name': 'add', 'arguments': {'a': 2, 'b': 3}}}]},
    {'role': 'tool', 'tool_call_id': 'call_1', 'name': 'add', 'content': '5'},
    {'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'It is 5.'},
]
_oai = LlamaChat.hist2fmt(_h)
test_eq(_oai[2], {'role': 'tool', 'tool_call_id': 'call_1', 'name': 'add', 'content': '5'})
test_eq(_oai[1]['tool_calls'][0]['function']['arguments'], '{"a": 2, "b": 3}')   # args JSON-encoded for llama.cpp
test_eq(LlamaChat.fmt2hist(_h), _h)                                               # no-op on already-canonical dicts
```

`comp_kw` overrides the sampling settings, so a key the chat also sets,
such as `temperature`, is replaced instead of raising a
duplicate-argument error.

``` python
class _Eng:
    def create_chat_completion(self, msgs, **kw): self.kw = kw

c = LlamaChat.__new__(LlamaChat)
c.engine, c._samp, c.max_output_tokens, c.toolspecs = _Eng(), {'temperature': .2}, None, []
c.comp_kw, c._msgs = {'temperature': .9, 'stop': ['x']}, lambda: []
c._step()
test_eq(c.engine.kw['temperature'], .9)
c.engine.kw['stop']
```

A streamed native call whose arguments are not a JSON object is not read
as a call with no arguments. `_stream_step` marks the call `unread` and
sets `tool_parse_failed`, so the tool loop asks the model to send it
again, and the stored call renders into the next prompt as an empty
argument object.

``` python
class _SEng:
    n_tokens = 5
    def create_chat_completion(self, msgs, **kw):
        d = lambda tc: {'choices': [{'delta': {'tool_calls': tc}, 'finish_reason': None}]}
        yield d([{'index': 0, 'id': 'a', 'function': {'name': 'add', 'arguments': '{"a": 1'}}])
        yield d([{'index': 1, 'id': 'b', 'function': {'name': 'add', 'arguments': '{"a": 1, "b": 2}'}}])
        yield {'choices': [{'delta': {}, 'finish_reason': 'tool_calls'}]}

c = LlamaChat.__new__(LlamaChat)
c.engine, c._samp, c.max_output_tokens, c.toolspecs = _SEng(), {}, None, []
c.comp_kw, c.turn_msg, c._sys_msgs, c._cache_dirty, c.hist = {}, None, lambda: [], True, []
c.count_tokens, c._note_cache = (lambda t: 0), (lambda u, cached: u)
list(c._stream_step())
bad, good = c._step_res['tool_calls']
test_eq((bad.get('unread'), good.get('unread')), (True, None))
test_eq((bad['function']['arguments'], good['function']['arguments']), ({}, {'a': 1, 'b': 2}))
assert c._step_res['tool_parse_failed']
c.hist = [c._step_res]
[(t['function']['arguments'], 'unread' in t) for t in c._msgs()[0]['tool_calls']]
```

## Examples (manual)

These cells load real weights and are marked `#| eval: false`. The test
run skips them. The output shown was saved from an earlier run. For
ordinary chat, tools, streaming, classification and structured output,
use the calls on the [index](index.html) page with a `-GGUF` repo id.
The examples here show what only this backend does: reusing the KV
cache, and image and audio input through `mmproj`.

The first example counts the tokens llama.cpp evaluates on each turn.
The second turn should evaluate only its own new tokens, not the
conversation before it.

``` python
# Real llama.cpp KV-prefix test: instrument `eval` to see how many tokens are actually evaluated.
# On turn two the first eval batch should contain only the new tail, not the cached conversation.
kvchat = LlamaChat(qwen3_06b, think=False, temp=0.0, max_output_tokens=16)
seen, orig_eval = [], kvchat.engine.eval
def counted_eval(tokens):
    seen.append(len(tokens))
    return orig_eval(tokens)
kvchat.engine.eval = counted_eval
try:
    kvchat(('cache verification context ' * 96) + '\nReply with exactly: stored')
    context_before_turn2 = kvchat.engine.n_tokens
    seen.clear()
    r = kvchat('What exact word did I ask you to reply with? Reply with only that word.')
    assert seen, 'llama.cpp never evaluated the second prompt'
    second_tail = seen[0]
    print(dict(context_before_turn2=context_before_turn2, second_tail_evaluated=second_tail,
               reported_cached=kvchat.use.cached_tokens, answer=resp_text(r)))
    assert second_tail < context_before_turn2, 'turn two re-evaluated the full prior context; KV prefix reuse missed'
    assert kvchat.use.cached_tokens > 0, kvchat.use
    assert 'stored' in resp_text(r).lower(), resp_text(r)
finally:
    kvchat.engine.eval = orig_eval
    kvchat.close()
```

### Streaming and thinking

`stream=True` yields markdown as on every backend, with the model’s
thinking as a blockquote and each tool call as a line starting with ⏳.
Urai’s `display_stream` renders it live in a notebook, as on the
LiteRT-LM backend. With a Qwen3 model, `think=True` turns thinking on.

### Images and audio (mmproj)

A vision or audio GGUF comes as the model plus an `mmproj` projector.
Pass `mmproj=True` and rishi fetches the projector from the same repo.
Then mix text with `bytes` or `Path` values in the prompt list. rishi
turns them into `image_url` and `input_audio` parts, and the patched
handler encodes them in the order they appear.

The examples describe an image and transcribe a clip with Gemma 4 E2B.
The last one loads Ultravox, whose projector has an audio encoder and no
vision encoder, which is the case the `_init_mtmd_context` patch exists
for.

``` python
# downloads the model *and* its mmproj projector once, then loads both from cache
vchat = LlamaChat('unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF', mmproj=True)
r = vchat(['Describe this image.', Path('images.jpeg')])   # raw bytes work too
print(resp_text(r))
vchat.close()
```

``` python
uvchat = LlamaChat('ggml-org/ultravox-v0_5-llama-3_2-1b-GGUF', mmproj=True)
assert resp_text(uvchat(['Transcribe this clip.', Path('speech.wav')])).strip()
uvchat.close()
```

``` python
img = Path('images.jpeg').read_bytes()
m = _mk_msg([img, 'what is this?'])
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.gguf') as f:
    test_eq(MTMDChatHandler(f.name, verbose=False).get_image_urls([m]), [m['content'][0]['image_url']['url']])
test_eq(m['content'][1], {'type': 'text', 'text': 'what is this?'})
test_eq(_mk_content(Path('images.jpeg')), _mk_content(img))   # a Path is read and sniffed like bytes

# audio is no longer refused - it becomes an OpenAI `input_audio` part
p = _mk_content(Path('speech.wav'))
test_eq((p['type'], p['input_audio']['format']), ('input_audio', 'wav'))
```

### Stopping with an LLM judge

When a model writes Python code blocks for Urai to run, Urai’s
`PyFenceCallback` runs each block and shows the model the output. It
repeats this until its `done(chat)` function returns True or the model
writes no more code. `output_matches(expected)` builds a `done` that
stops once the last code output contains `expected`. `task_complete`
asks the model instead, through `chat.classify`, whether the
conversation has done what was asked. `done` can be any function that
takes the chat and returns a bool, including one that consults a second,
stronger chat. Both helpers live in `urai.sandbox` and work with every
backend; see Urai’s
[sandbox](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/sandbox.html) page.

## Sharing one engine

A loaded `Llama` belongs to one process, and loading the same model in
several programs wastes memory.
[`LlamaBroker`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/llama.html#llamabroker)
loads it once in a long-lived process and serves it over a Unix socket.
Each client gets its own
[`LlamaChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/llama.html#llamachat)
and history, and all of them share one copy of the weights. The protocol
and the client are Urai’s `ChatBroker`, described on Urai’s
[broker](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/broker.html) page.
